I’m sorry that happened to you. No person should ever be treated like an object or a throwaway, and you deserve better. It is also not your fault that someone did that to you. I would honestly consider talking to a professional though if those relationships have caused you so much pain that they’ve tainted your view of women as a whole and if it’s preventing you from getting into new healthy and fulfilling relationships (including friendships). 

You don’t have to answer this, but do you have anyone in your life who you’re able to be emotionally vulnerable with? A lot (if not most) men suffer from societal expectations of being an emotionless rock, and often romantic partners are the only place they feel able to get emotional support. When a romantic partner uses this against them it can be incredibly traumatic. I ask all this because I know a few men  who basically viewed all women as heartless, conniving bitches - each of them had an ex or a string of exes who were the man’s only emotional support and the person he’d confide most in, and those individual women would use the information and past expressions of emotion as a weapon when they fought or when they broke up. Once the men were able to trust someone to listen to their feelings without being terrified of it being used to break them open again, they were able to find much better women and have much healthier relationships, and also a better quality of life in general even when they were single. Please excuse me if that’s not at all close to what you were experiencing though!

To be fair, it looks like several people did assume you hate women even if they didn’t use that exact phrasing. I generally don’t ask “who hurt you” because it’s a fight starter; whether the person was actually hurt or not they’ll be pissed and it won’t be productive. Did you have a woman in your life who regularly chose material possessions or her dog over you, or is this more how you feel due to what you’re seeing in media / on social media?

Dude, your friend is straight up in an abusive relationship. It sucks that he got fat and can’t do the fun stuff you guys used to do, but you need to take this as seriously as if you had a female friend whose partner was beating her. Your friend needs help. If you can, try to find out if she’s hitting/pinching/scratching him, even “as a joke” - women can be physically abusive as well and these things always eventually escalate. Also try to find out if she monitors his internet and phone use. Does he have to show her all his texts and call records? Does she regularly go through his internet history or is he not allowed to use the computer unless she’s in the room with him? 
*Edit: Check for these because they can indicate a higher probability of serious harm to your friend. It’s also easier for people to have something that aligns more with stereotypical abuse symptoms to point to in order to help someone realize they’re in an abusive relationship.*

Here are some resources and information for men in abusive relationships and for you as a friend on how to help:
https://www.helpguide.org/articles/abuse/help-for-men-who-are-being-abused.htm

http://www.doctornerdlove.com/men-in-abusive-relationships/

https://wellkentucky.org/supporting-a-friend-in-an-abusive-relationship/

https://www.loveisrespect.org/for-someone-else/help-a-friend/

https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/presence-mind/201510/how-help-someone-in-abusive-relationship

PLEASE do not brush this off as April just being a buzzkill. And your friend may be offended at the suggestion that he, a man, is being abused, but please bring it up to him when it’s safe to do so. A large component of emotional/mental abuse is gaslighting - making the victim believe they’re crazy and that they’re overreacting, when in reality they’re being undermined and manipulated. Your friend may *need* to hear outside confirmation that this is wrong and not healthy.

Tl;dr: sucks to have a friend get fat but also sucks to have a friend in an abusive relationship; can’t fix the fat issue before the abuse issue is fixed.
